title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement correctly separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow is a program that uses no language model, and an agent is one that uses a model
A workflow is limited to a fixed list of tools, and an agent may be given any number of tools
A workflow is a program that calls no tools, and an agent is one that calls tools
A workflow has its steps set by code in advance, and an agent has its next step chosen by the model

items.stem: A makerspace program handles each booking request in the same way: it calls the model to pull the machine and date out of the message, then its own code calls check_calendar, then it calls the model again to write the reply the student reads. How should this program be classified?

options.text: A workflow, because the code fixes the sequence even though the model is called twice
An agent, because the model is called more than once for a single request
An agent, because the program uses a tool to read the booking calendar
An agent, because the model writes the reply that the student finally reads

items.stem: Your team wants predictable behavior and the lowest model cost for one feature of the makerspace assistant. Which feature is the best candidate for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Helping a student work out why a 3D print keeps failing halfway through
Choosing a fix for a laser cutter fault that the student describes only vaguely
The day before each booking: look it up, fill in a reminder template and send it
Planning a multi-machine project for a student who has a rough idea only

items.stem: The assistant must handle two kinds of request: booking requests and open-ended troubleshooting questions about failed prints. Your team has a small model budget. Which structure is best to defend at the design review?

options.text: Code routes bookings through a fixed workflow and sends troubleshooting questions to an agent
One agent with every tool handles both kinds, since an agent can do what a workflow does
One fixed workflow handles both kinds, with extra steps added for the troubleshooting cases
An agent reads every request first and decides for itself whether to run the booking steps

items.stem: In one sentence, why does an agent usually cost more per request than a workflow that does the same job?

In testing, your booking agent sometimes creates a booking without calling check_training_record, although its instructions say to call it first. Every booking must include that check. Which change best fixes this?

options.text: Rewrite the instructions to state the training rule more forcefully and put it first
Move the booking steps into fixed code that always runs the training check first
Switch to a larger model that follows written instructions more reliably
Add a second model call that reviews each booking and asks the agent to redo it
